newsitem.title: FRANCE: AGF sees little impact from Chunnel fire.
newsitem.headline: AGF sees little impact from Chunnel fire.

text.p: The Channel Tunnel fire on Monday will have little impact on Assurances Generales de France (AGF), which is re-insured and whose exposure is limited to 10.5 percent of property damage and operating loss, a spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"The fire will have a modest impact because AGF is re-insured and our risk is only 10.5 percent," she told Reuters.

AGF is co-insurer for the Channel Tunnel and its operator, Eurotunnel, along with primary insurer Union des Assurances de Paris. They are partly exposed to infrastructure damage and operating losses by the company.
A source close to Eurotunnel estimated the cost of the damage at tens of millions of pounds sterling.
UAP has said it was too early to evaluate the impact on its accounts.

A spokeswoman for re-insurer Scor said on Friday that the cost of the fire to the group was expected to run between five and 10 million francs. But the company said it did not expect the fire to have an impact on this year's results.
U.S. group Chubb Corp insures rolling stock in the sub-sea tunnel.
